labels.2: Multi-Agent Code Generation for Scientific Analysis
labels.6: Security and Vulnerabilities in Code Generation

descriptions.0: These papers focus on improving the decoding process of diffusion language models (DLMs), particularly through parallel decoding strategies, token selection, and architectural modifications. They address challenges such as efficiency, quality, and coordination of updates in masked diffusion models.
descriptions.1: These papers unify around using evolutionary algorithms guided by large language models to optimize system prompts, heuristics, or planning patterns. They leverage self-referential or metacognitive mechanisms to iteratively improve solutions through cycles of generation, evaluation, and reflection.
descriptions.2: These papers unify around using multi-agent LLM systems to automate complex scientific and engineering analysis tasks, generating executable code from natural language or visual inputs. They employ specialized sub-agents for task decomposition, code synthesis, verification, and debugging to produce reproducible workflows.
descriptions.3: These papers propose multi-agent or self-evolving systems that use LLMs for adaptive code generation, often incorporating structured communication, iterative refinement, and test-time scaling. They unify around the idea of orchestrating specialized agents or modules to autonomously generate, execute, and improve code for complex tasks.
descriptions.4: These papers focus on benchmarking and evaluating code agents, particularly in interactive and multi-round settings, and analyzing their behavior in real-world scenarios such as pull requests. They introduce new benchmarks (Asuka-Bench, WebIGBench) and empirical studies (AI-usage in GitHub, rejection of agentic PRs) to understand and improve code generation agents.
descriptions.5: This cluster focuses on evaluating and improving code generation by LLMs, including benchmarks (PowerCodeBench, CodeGolf Bench, TeleSWEBench, SWE-InfraBench, NovelAPIBench), methods for enhancing correctness and conciseness (RLVR, demand-guided intervention, preference-based MaxSAT), and analyzing factors affecting output (prompt cues, knowledge boundaries). The papers share a common goal of advancing reliable and efficient code generation through systematic evaluation and targeted interventions.
descriptions.6: These papers focus on security aspects of LLM-based code generation, including vulnerabilities introduced by prompt perturbations, self-play for secure code, knowledge activation for security, grammar-constrained decoding risks, backdoor detection, and hallucination patterns. They collectively address how to generate secure code and detect or mitigate vulnerabilities in generated code.
